title: Variables [Walruses]
description:
_I'm sorry, what is that lesson title?_
In Go, there is the sad variable decl:
```go
var bad int
bad = 12345
```
But, there is a _actually good way:_
```go
bad := 12345
```
Both of those do the same thing. The walrus operator (`:=`) both declares _and assigns_ to a variable in one line. Go infers the type of `bad` as int because the `12345` value.
## Why/When the walrus operator
The Walrus operator should be used to write less code (duh), and should be used instead of `var` whenever possible, but there is only one problem: It can _only be used in a function_.
